claims.statement: The workflow covers OpenWiki, Deep Agents Python, Deep Agents Code, and Deep Agents JS through a product registry that assigns each product its upstream repository, documentation paths, product skill, release tag prefix, and product-specific memory file.

The release selector fetches GitHub releases, excludes drafts and prereleases, filters by the registered tag prefix, and selects the newest release published between `min_age_days` and `max_age_days` ago, returning the preceding eligible release when available; its defaults are 7 and 30 days.

The operating instructions require every run to load the product skill, use a 7-to-30-day release window, stop when no eligible or unshipped work exists, inspect only the configured documentation scope, and split needed updates into individual features.

Product skills distinguish user-facing documentation candidates from normally skipped internal, dependency-only, or behavior-neutral changes, and define product-specific documentation scope and language guidance.

The deployed product schedules run on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday in the `America/Los_Angeles` timezone at 09:00 for OpenWiki, 09:30 for Deep Agents Python, 10:00 for Deep Agents Code, and 10:30 for Deep Agents JS.
The shipping skill requires one feature per focused branch, Linear issue, and draft PR; a release containing multiple features must invoke the workflow separately for each feature.

A Linear issue is created in the resolved team with product and optional release metadata, is assigned to the authenticated Linear viewer unless an active configured override is used, and remote HTTP, GraphQL, or creation failures raise errors.
Durable memory is a deployment-shared, read/write agent-scoped tree whose hot `AGENTS.md` is loaded on every run and whose content persists in LangSmith Context Hub across deployments.
The instructions limit durable memory to procedural release tracking—product, tag, feature, Linear URL, PR URL, and dates—and forbid storing personal data, secrets, tokens, or credentials.
Because every caller shares agent-scoped memory and future runs receive hot memory, the implementation treats that memory as untrusted input and keeps tool authority and approvals outside it.

The deployment authenticates callers with LangSmith API-key authentication, while GitHub and Linear tools resolve agent-owned connection secrets with local environment fallbacks; public GitHub release reads can continue anonymously when credentials are unavailable or rejected.
Adding coverage requires a registry entry, a matching product skill, and a schedule prompt, followed by redeployment.
Draft PR creation sends `draft: true`, and the project README states that humans review draft PRs before merge.

The release-research subagent has only read tools and is instructed to return a JSON feature report after comparing releases, confirming tagged source, and checking current documentation; the main agent must invoke it before its Linear or draft-PR write tools.

Research treats release notes as secondary leads: it uses the previous same-prefix tag for the source comparison when possible, scopes changed files to configured source prefixes, and requires tagged-source confirmation before a feature needs documentation.

Both Linear issue and draft-PR tools require non-empty source evidence naming a repository, release tag, and cited path plus symbol or quote, verify each citation against the tagged upstream file, and add a Source evidence section when absent from the body.

Draft-PR creation rejects missing or no-op edit entries and paths under `docs-release-watch/`; for each file it fetches the base branch, accepts an exact base match, or rebases a stale edit only when its changed hunks can be applied uniquely.

Although `tools/docs_edit.py` supplies 35% line-churn and language-fence validation helpers, `create_draft_docs_pr` imports only its stale-edit rebase helper, neither invokes those validators nor exposes a product or language-scope parameter, so churn and language-fence checks are not enforced in the PR creation path.
Draft PR creation targets `langchain-ai/docs`, normalizes a branch to `docs/…`, creates blobs, a tree, and a commit from the requested base branch, then requests a pull request with `draft: True`.

The focused evidence tests cover evidence shape, no-op and base-content rules, stale-edit rebasing, source-prefix filtering, line-churn calculation, a rejected language-fence edit, and ship-failure-section replacement, but do not call the end-to-end PR creation operation.

The GitHub Actions Linear synchronization job runs only for same-repository pull requests on opened, reopened, draft-conversion, ready-for-review, and closed events; it skips successfully when `LINEAR_API_KEY` is absent and passes PR lifecycle fields to the synchronization script.

The PR-to-Linear script activates only for the `Closes DOC-N` convention, maps draft, ready, merged, and unmerged-closed PR states to team workflow states by preferred name with a type fallback, and fails an intended sync when no target state exists.

`create_draft_docs_pr` documents the `Closes [DOC-N](linear-url)` body convention but does not parse or require it, so a successful draft-PR call does not by itself guarantee later Linear lifecycle synchronization.

If a Linear issue was created but draft-PR creation still fails after one fresh-file retry, the operating instructions require `note_ship_failure_on_linear_issue`; that tool updates the issue description with a replaceable Ship failure section and creates a failure comment with a LangSmith run URL when available.
